column4: sunset sky, low sun, flat-shaded blocks, palms, striped kerbs, neon strips, yellow IT marker, patient with gown on the IT vehicle
built to the 90s arcade test shot; town, cast and map are original (evidence/nearest-game.txt)
3D chase camera above and behind; field of view widens with speed
grip 9 normally, 1.5 with Space held, recovering over drift_recover; feel itself is for the person's play
a ram at tag_min_speed passes the patient; the old IT is immune for tagback_grace; play.png shows a tag landed
fire engine (heavy, slow) and cruiser (light, quick) with their own stats in config.js, labelled (bot) on the HUD
5 by 5 street grid, 16 blocks, a plaza with a fountain, one north-south and one east-west alley
three rounds, round clock and scoreboard on play.png, star rating on the results screen
engine, siren and crunch are built with Web Audio; no check can hear them
six civilian cars keep right round the grid and pull to the kerb within civ_pullover_range of a responder
tag by collision, chase and crash, built for real
bot driver: chases with routing and lead when IT, flees by junction when not
there and wired: civilians collide with everyone and yield to sirens
round 1 starts the ambulance at the junction (0,-60)
dispatch line naming who has Mr. Crouch shows as the round starts
Engine 9 starts IT 120 m up the same street, facing you
the fire engine reached and rammed the ambulance in the scripted run; the handbrake is on Space
the marker moved to the player and the banner says ram someone; chasing the cruiser down needs a person driving
on a tag the patient arcs from the old roof to the new one over 0.55 s
round 1 bots use 78% speed and 65% steering and do not lead their aim
round 3: corner cutting by line of sight to the next junction, a last-moment jink, and the leader looks 45 m closer to an IT bot
IT at the buzzer restarts that round; earlier rounds' totals are kept
